newsitem.title: DUBAI: United States and UAE end two-week Gulf war games.
newsitem.headline: United States and UAE end two-week Gulf war games.

text.p: The United States and the United Arab Emirates on Monday ended two weeks of naval exercises in the Gulf, a U.S. Navy spokesman said.
He said about 1,500 navy and marine corps troops took part.

"(It's a) routine exercise...a joint, combined field training exercise designed to enhance the capabilities and cooperation in combined arms operations between U.S...forces and the armed forces of the UAE," the spokesman told Reuters.
He said there were no reports of accidents during the exercise, which began on July 22.
He would not say how many UAE forces were involved in the war games, codenamed "Iron Magic '97". UAE officials were not immediately available for comment.

The exercises included three U.S. amphibious vessels. The assault ship Boxer, transport dock Ogden and landing craft Fort Fisher have been in the Gulf since May 20 and would remain for an unspecified period, the spokesman said earlier.

The UAE and the United States concluded a military pact in 1994 but full implementation has been hindered by obstacles including such issues as which country's laws would apply if U.S. military personnel committed a civil offence in the UAE.
U.S. naval forces patrolling the Gulf often come to the UAE and defence sources say as many as 40,000 U.S. servicemen visit the country every year.
